comments.value: The Unity Job System was not added until Unity 2018.1. VRChat is currently using Unity 2017.4.15f1 so it does not have the Job System.

I don't mind people putting up a feature request but if you look at the voter names then 75% are obviously manipulated

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}

You'll always need the limit because then artists will just ram into the performance limit with even more dynamic bones to see what is possible. Replacing it with a more efficient version of the same thing is still good so that a lot of existing avatars' hair can work again by default.

@{5c540514d859d512a8d1d2f9|full_name}: tbh, I think most don't even take what sort of performance impact dynamic bones have into consideration. As a result, having no limiter but a more performance friendly version would just lead to performance enhancements rather than people trying to add MORE dynamic bones

VRChat currently uses Unity 2017.4 LTS, which does not have the Jobs system.

Jobs (and ECS) were introduced in Unity 2018, which does not have an LTS version yet-- therefore, we have not looked into upgrading versions yet.

Once Unity 2018 LTS is out, we can begin migration to it. Once that is complete, we can look into Jobs/Hybrid ECS for various components, including DB.

This post will remain open, but I am making this post to let voters know that it is not possible right now, nor will it be possible until we get to 2018 LTS.
@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: thank you kindly informations! I agree with your suggestions. When unity2018 LTS is out and migration , I will  remember this issue.
@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: 2018 lts is out :)  how is progress
Related: [Make Dynamic bones limit disabled by default](https://vrchat.canny.io/feature-requests/p/make-dynamic-bones-limit-disabled-by-default)
@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: so about that job system was it done yet?

@{5f47de17bc82ac1e0f90f607|full_name}: Turns out that parallelization doesn't help much when the underlying methods aren't that performant to start with, and when the methods act on objects that depend on other objects in the hierarchy. When getting f(n) requires knowing the result of f(n-1) first, you can't make it parallel effectively.
tl;dr: we looked into it, it isn't as easy as anyone had hoped, and simply "using jobs" doesn't really do that much. We'll circle back around to it eventually!
@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: got ya thank you for the info <3
This request is addressed via the new addition of PhysBones, which are much (much) faster than DynamicBones!
